summary: The candidate is correct with its stated constants, hypotheses, and quantifiers. Small and degenerate cases, including r=q=0, zero rank with retained coordinates, singleton threshold sets, zero or repeated rows, rows inactive at the selected vector, k=0, zero projection, zero profile values, cap boundaries, and threshold ties, do not refute it and are covered by the proof. The rank rounding argument preserves every original nonnegative form and loses at most the matrix rank times log(3). The maximal-determinant basis argument correctly proves that the coordinate maxima of the normalized active rows sum to at most q, without requiring a nonnegative rank factorization. The squared-row span has dimension at most q(q+1)/2, so the two rounding stages have exactly the asserted upper bound q(q+5)/2 on their total loss. The projected second-moment estimate controls all indexed rows simultaneously with probability at least one half using only a union bound over the two signs. The supplied capped finite-set estimate and integer moment estimates apply with their exact definitions and independent scopes. Finite log-concavity, the weighted-band argument, and the original-center injection preserve the exact threshold and all original weights. Both numerical coefficient bounds follow from the displayed hand inequalities. Finally, finite attainment and the original oriented-curvature comparison give K(w) at least Corner(w), and the supplied fixed-center actual-body theorem supplies one point before the halfspace with all the stated depth bounds. No mathematical errors or gaps were found.
